The device is an expandable heart valve designed for implantation in the pulmonary position in children with congenital heart disease. Unlike conventional prostheses, which must be replaced as the child grows, this valve incorporates a stent frame that can be dilated by balloon catheter in stages, up to a maximum diameter of 26 mm. In a prospective study of 63 patients aged 2 to 17, freedom from device-related reintervention at 24 months was 92 percent. Hemodynamic performance was maintained after dilation, with mean gradients below 15 mmHg in 95 percent of cases. Adverse events included endocarditis in two patients and stent fracture in one. The agency approved the device with a requirement for a ten-year post-approval study.
